title: The All-City Team
basis: 2026 preseason consensus, compiled before Week 1 kickoff.

rules.public_summary: Rule: the player's own first or last name must be exactly the name of a place its state classifies as a city. Towns, villages, boroughs and unincorporated communities do not count, and neither do partial matches. Tier is the 2020 census count and nothing else: 100,000 and up is a Marquee City, 5,000 to 99,999 is a City, under 5,000 is a Technical Qualifier.
rules.verification_note: City class and population checked against each municipality's census entry on 2026-08-31.
full_rules: Exact match only. The player's first name or last name, standing alone, must equal the city's commonly used proper name. No nicknames, no spelling variants, no partial matches, no words merely contained inside a longer city name: a player named York qualifies for York, Pennsylvania and gets nothing from New York.
The name must be one whole token of the player's name. Hyphenated and compound surnames count as one name; Smith-Njigba is not Smith, and St. Brown is not Brown.
Generational suffixes are not names. Jr., Sr., II, III, IV and V are stripped before matching.

The place must be an incorporated municipality that its own state classifies as a CITY. This is the bright line that keeps the feature from becoming an argument about size: the test is the charter rather than the headcount, so a 396-person city is in and a 278-person town stays a town.

The four countries in play are the United States, France, the United Kingdom and Sweden, matching the league's own nationalities. The default rule is the U.S. one; an allied city is used only where no U.S. city carries the name.

Washington, D.C. needs no special exception. Washington, Pennsylvania is an incorporated city of 13,176, so the name clears the default rule without anyone having to rule on the District's municipal status.
Team names, stadium names and nicknames are worth nothing.
considered_and_rejected: A population floor. It would have been arbitrary at every value we tried, and it would have thrown out Aubrey, Texas, which the premise specifically wanted in.
A named Washington, D.C. exception. Unnecessary; see above.
Counting incorporated places of any class. That admits Gibbs, Missouri (village, 70 people) and hands the roster the consensus RB1, which is a better lineup and a worse rule.

cross_checks.finding: Orders the board Gibbs, Robinson, Chase, Taylor, then Smith-Njigba, with Cook 9th, Jefferson 13th and London 15th. Agrees with the FantasyPros snapshot on every player this feature uses, which is why no single-analyst ranking is doing any work here.

starters.assessment: QB1 on both consensus boards and the highest-ranked quarterback in the superflex file at overall rank 1. Active, first on the depth chart, no injury designation.

sources.label: Allen, Texas
sources.quote: Allen is a city in Collin County in the U.S. state of Texas, and a northern suburb in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. Incorporated 1953; population 104,627 at the 2020 census.

starters.research_notes: Replaces Lamar Jackson from the candidate lineup. Jackson also qualifies (Jackson, Mississippi) and is QB2 on both boards; Allen is ahead on both, so the slot goes to Allen. Allen is the only starter that clears the 100,000 marquee line, which is its own joke given that Dallas is on the bench.

starters.assessment: Second overall on the FantasyPros board and first on Sleeper's. Active, first on the depth chart, no injury designation.

He hyperextended his left knee in a practice on 2026-08-25 and still carried a Questionable tag in the 2026-08-30 sync; he told reporters that if there were a game the next day he would play, and reporting through 2026-08-31 has him on track for the opener.

sources.label: Chase knee injury reporting, late August 2026

sources.label: Jefferson, Georgia
sources.quote: Jefferson is a city and the county seat of Jackson County, Georgia, United States. Incorporated as a town in 1806 and as a city in 1896; population 13,233 at the 2020 census.

starters.research_notes: Jefferson City, Missouri is a compound name and does not count. Jefferson, Georgia is the cleanest qualifier: county seat, chartered as a city in 1896. Replaces Parker Washington, who is WR30 at overall 65.

starters.assessment: TE3 on both boards behind Bowers and McBride, at overall 40. Age-22 season, first on the Chicago depth chart, no injury designation. The role is locked and the sample is one year, so the ceiling is doing some of the work here.

sources.label: Loveland, Colorado
sources.quote: Loveland is a home rule municipality and the second most populous municipality in Larimer County, Colorado. Listed as a home rule city; incorporated April 30, 1881; population 76,378 at the 2020 census.

starters.research_notes: The weakest starter, and he is still TE3 in football. Replaces Dallas Goedert, who is TE12 at overall 116. Tyler Warren (Warren, Michigan) is TE4 at overall 52 and is the fallback if Loveland's role changes.

starters.assessment: K1 on both boards by a real margin: 202nd overall against 206 for the next kicker on FantasyPros, and 92nd against 118 on Sleeper's. Active, first on the depth chart, no injury designation.

sources.label: Aubrey, Texas
sources.quote: Aubrey is a city in Denton County, Texas, United States. Its population was 5,006 at the 2020 census; a 2025 estimate puts it at 9,066.

starters.research_notes: Confirmed as an incorporated city, which the brief flagged as the open question. At 5,006 it clears the Technical Qualifier ceiling by six residents. The candidate lineup flagged Aubrey's incorporation as the open question; it is settled.
